write_up: I read this for Software Engineer roles. You have a computer science degree, an internship at Cardinal Health, and projects that use the same web technologies. It's common for a new graduate's resume to lean on duties and team activities, but those lines won't stand out in a pile when a recruiter can't see what you built.

The Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model: it names the application, its purpose, and the tools you used. Your experience includes both the internship and the help desk role, so move Experience above Education. The objective names the job you want, but the rest of it could describe almost any graduate.

Let's start with the Cardinal Health inventory application. Name the features you developed, then use the testing and bug-fix lines to show what you worked on. Keep the project details that name what you built, and replace the soft-skills list with examples in your work.
